analysis.title: Consumer Confidence Unexpectedly Improved in October
key_insights: Conference Board consumer confidence rose 6.7 points to 91.7 in October after three straight monthly declines. It was well above the consensus forecast of 81.0 and the highest since June 2026.
Confidence is still down 4.0% from a year earlier despite the October increase.
The present situation index rose 8.6 points to 120.4, the highest since April 2026. The expectations index rose 6.9 points to 72.6, its first improvement in four months.

The labor market differential (share saying jobs are plentiful minus share saying jobs are hard to get) rose 2.4 points to +5.3%. The gain came entirely from more consumers saying jobs are plentiful, while jobs hard to get was unchanged.

Only consumers under 35 and households with income of $100k+ reported higher confidence. Confidence rose across the political spectrum, but much more for Republicans. Gen Z and Millennials remain the most confident generations.
Consumers plan to spend less on durable goods and services over the next six months, possibly because higher prices and elevated inflation have reduced disposable income.
Median one-year-ahead inflation expectations fell to 4.7% from 5.1% in September but remain elevated. Consumers expect interest rates to rise over the next year.
PNC expects real consumer spending to rise at a 3.5% annual rate in Q3, supported by modest job gains and a still-low jobless rate. The GDP report is due Thursday.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up 6.7 points from September and well above the 81.0 consensus. It is the first rise after three monthly declines and the highest level since June 2026.
The actual reading beat consensus by about 10.7 points.
Up 8.6 points, the highest since April 2026, reflecting better assessments of current labor market and business conditions.
Up 6.9 points, the first improvement in four months.
Up 2.4 points as more consumers said jobs are plentiful. The report's Figure 2 caption says the differential suggests pressure on the unemployment rate.
Down from 5.1% in September but still elevated. Consumers expect interest rates to rise over the next year.
PNC's forecast, ahead of the GDP report due Thursday. It is supported by modest job gains and a low jobless rate.

risk_factors: Inflation expectations remain elevated at 4.7%, and consumers expect interest rates to rise over the next year.
Higher prices and elevated inflation may be reducing disposable income, and consumers plan to spend less on durable goods and services over the next six months.
The improvement in confidence was narrow by demographic group: only those under 35 and households earning $100k+ reported gains.
The labor market differential is described as suggesting pressure on the unemployment rate.
